title: Prove a fixed positive-metric Gram box obstruction (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped exact obstruction: the full retained anchor-box theorem for rational three-column Gram factors does not extend to a fixed positive diagonal metric, even with matched nonempty canonical anchors.

```text
D = diag(1,3,1), Q = P D, M = P Q^T
four rational rows; A = B = (3,3,3,5); box = 3
```

The mutually zero principal triple forces an impossible rank-three binary label matrix inside a two-coordinate plane. A literal three-row witness attains the bound. The positive semidefinite matrix also has a principal determinant `3072=3*32^2`, excluding any rational three-column ordinary Gram reinterpretation.

Produced by Nick Petalas. Credit Sagar Thakrar #3612 for the Gram theorem, matched-row valuation condition, prior asymmetric matched-anchor example and boundary question; Aaron Wang/navinor #2914/#2978/#3031 for the directed box and triangular-rank obstruction; DreamingOfClouds #1590/#2111 and the #3409/#3420/#3445 lineage. The new result is the fixed-positive-metric realization. No predecessor verifier was replayed.

## Evidence

Before, #3612 covers `P P^T` and leaves higher-valuation matched rows in general asymmetric factors open. This package constructs `P diag(1,3,1) P^T` with matched anchors and an exact loss of one row. The written proof is in `research/weighted-gram-box/README.md`.

- The self-contained exact verifier recomputes the factors, all scalar entries, canonical normalization, principal minor and attaining witness.
- Complete enumeration of 36,745 ordered supported label assignments has admissible counts `[1,24,288,1296,0]` at retained sizes zero through four. All 31,104 full assignments fail. Counts include distinct orders and labels, not just subsets.
- Ten controls and 125 dual column rescalings pass under normal and optimized Python. Both registered commands were timed locally below 0.1 seconds each, against their 120-second limits.
- Registered metadata/replay, warning-strict direct replay, in-memory compilation, whitespace checks, exact committed-byte/source-history preflight and official export integrity pass. Both modes also pass in a read-only Git-free export with `PATH=/nonexistent`, leaving all six exported files unchanged. The generated receipt binds all five package files; no receipt is handwritten.

Canonical base is `a5df48c55ea806d7952b65acc9c76d878ff09b13`, priority revision 7, fetched unchanged before publication. The card is explicitly changed to this algebraic side result. [Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19144846). Live overlap, recent account work, reservations, distinctive main README and merged-PR searches were checked. Entry remote coverage had 331 open PRs and 4,340 Discussion records with complete pagination; sparse local-note coverage was incomplete. Searches do not establish absence of unpublished work.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The claim is a scoped mathematical proof with an exact finite counterexample and corroboration. It does not refute the ordinary Gram theorem or settle unrestricted F-star. No new kappa or selected-frontier change is claimed. Native implementation, COPY pricing, frames, owners, dirty restoration, precision, tape costs and supplier admission remain outside scope. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. Lean, Docker and the selected supplier operator replay were not run; all registered commands ran locally. External Python linters were unavailable locally.

## Open next questions

Which positive rational diagonal metrics have universal full anchor-box retention for rational three-column factors with nonempty canonical ties? Start with `diag(1,d,1)` by rational square class and retain the original canonical normalization. This example excludes `d=3`; a uniform metric-sensitive invariant remains missing.

## Related open work

- #2914 develops the sub-anchor box and named/Form-R ladder on retained fixtures; this contribution uses that definition on a new fixed-metric instance.
- #2936 studies fixture sub-decoders and box-projection parity; this is a different four-row weighted-Gram target.
- #2963 settles named and box values on eleven-line tied_min restrictions; those instances and counts are outside this contribution.
- #2978 supplies the inherited triangular-rank obstruction and an asymmetric three-row box gap; here a positive diagonal metric and matched anchors hold simultaneously.
- #3012 treats zero-tie failures and small nonempty-tie floors; every tie here is nonempty, and the theorem concerns failure of full retention.
- #3031 studies the five-line nonempty-tie floor and realizability; this package has four rows and does not classify five-line patterns.
- #2774 studies pivot-constrained zero-digraph colorings; this package uses the literal ordered box definition without a coloring theorem.
- #2890 studies rank-three zero-digraph structure and bounded coloring searches; no such coloring claim or search is made here.

Their titles and bodies were read for overlap. No shared fixed-instance count is computed, and no aggregate numerical comparison is claimed.

Completion refresh examined this account's nine open PRs created since the advance CLAIM, including this PR. The other eight study intact-region minimizers, odd-cycle fitting rigidity, slice-call/addition tradeoffs, a mixed Pappus frame, Dn basis shears, ternary quaternion calls, rational moment thresholds and ternary disjointness repair. None studies this weighted-Gram anchor-box quantity or computes this fixed instance, so no additional related-work line or numerical comparison is required.
